creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-11-09 on 0.24.0: a laptop window showing a maker pane on the devenv with two worker helpers, one on each machine's daemon, both mid-task. The folded line under the maker read `2 helpers · 2 done`, and the owner took it to mean both had finished. At the same moment `muster window --json` gave both helpers `state: working` (context 44% and 26%, both editing files).

Shortly before, the window had hung up in the middle of a `muster pane wait` ("the window ... hung up in the middle of the watch"), so the shell may have kept states from before it reconnected. A third helper, a reviewer, had been closed earlier; whether the line still counts it is not known. `SidebarModel.helpersLine` counts the helpers in the most urgent state among them, and `mostUrgent` ranks done above working, so the shell held both helpers as done while their daemons said working.

Possibly: find out whether the shell's helper states go stale across a window reconnect, or whether a closed helper is still counted. Separately, consider whether a folded line should prefer the live state over done, so it cannot read as "finished" while agents work.
title: A folded helpers line read 2 done while both helpers were working
